If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for bearish bias.  
If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon (day 8–15), reduce forecast by 2–4% for mid horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) in the last 3 days, apply a 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment for late horizon (16–30 days) to dampen volatility.  
If forecast exceeds true value by >3% in early horizon and sentiment is positive, subtract 1–2% from next forecast to correct for momentum overcorrection.  
If forecast is below true value by >3% in late horizon and sentiment is negative, add 1–2% to next forecast to counteract pessimism.
